title: Dagobert Renouf: Burnout, authentic posting, and building Launch Day as a community
summary: Dagobert Renouf explains how he grew on X by replying to people, then burned out and switched to being himself. He covers how Launch Day (48-hour launch events with big discounts and founder interviews) works, why community matters for solo makers, and why he stopped chasing money over vision.

principles.text: Early on, grow on social by replying to people daily and making friends; once big, switch to being yourself.
principles.quote: I used to do 250 replies a day for six months or one year

principles.text: Test demand with one tweet: if 20 people say yes with money, you have product-market fit.
principles.quote: you just make a tweet and you have 20 people say yeah take my money okay you know you have something

principles.text: Tell your story and show yourself: people who care about you then check out and buy your product.
principles.quote: what works is to show myself to tell my story then people give a [ __ ] and then they check out my product and they buy it

principles.text: Limited-time launch windows and deep, negotiated discounts create FOMO and drive buying.
principles.quote: if you don't limit people don't buy don't buy it. The limit helps people buy.

principles.text: Curate who you feature: pick founders who open up and give big discounts, and be honest when the audience is not a fit.
principles.quote: I don't accept people who's not going to give a big discount because they just want like to launch on 10 platforms

principles.text: Relying entirely on social media is fragile and stressful; an algorithm change can kill you.
principles.quote: when everything depends on social media then any change in algorithm can kill you that's very very uh stressful
